verbalization: Hydrocortisone, a corticosteroid, is implicated in the treatment of Acquired Angioedema, a condition characterized by swelling of the skin and mucous membranes. This relationship is supported by the evidence that Hydrocortisone is indicated for Acquired Angioedema, which in turn is indicated for Allergic Rhinitis. The indirect pathway suggests that Hydrocortisone may exert a modulatory effect on the inflammatory processes underlying Allergic Rhinitis through its anti-inflammatory properties, potentially by suppressing the release of mediators such as histamine or other pro-inflammatory substances. The presence of two distinct but overlapping pathways—both involving Hydrocortisone and Allergic Rhinitis—indicates a plausible mechanistic link, though the exact mechanism remains to be fully elucidated. The evidence is consistent with a role for Hydrocortisone in the management of allergic inflammation, though further studies are needed to confirm its direct therapeutic effect on Allergic Rhinitis.
